comments.body:
## /rebar-debug — Phase 1: proven root cause (RCA)

**Mechanism (confirmed at runtime).** `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp` has no `acli` install step,
so the built image ships without the Atlassian CLI on `PATH`. The reconciler's Jira transport
spawns `acli` by **bare name** — `_DEFAULT_ACLI_CMD = ["acli"]` in
`adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py`, run via `subprocess.Popen(full_cmd, ...)` in `_run_acli`
(no `shutil.which`/abs-path guard). When the binary is absent, `Popen` raises
`FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'acli'`. `bridge_check_access`'s
`STEP_CREATE` calls `client.create_issue()`, whose `except Exception` arm
(`access_check.py:237-241`) reports `reason=exception, detail=str(exc)` — surfacing the raw
`FileNotFoundError` string exactly as observed.

**Discriminating proof.**
- `grep -rn "acli\|atlassian" infra/compose/Dockerfile.*` → nothing; no image provisions `acli`.
- Runtime reproduction of the exact error with `acli` off `PATH`:
  `subprocess.Popen(['acli','--version'], env={'PATH':'/nonexistent'})` →
  `RAISED: "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'acli'"` — byte-for-byte the ticket's `detail`.
- This discriminates against the ruled-out rivals the ticket already excluded: credentials
  (`GET /rest/api/3/myself` → 200), connectivity, and project scope are all proven good; the
  failure is specifically the missing `acli` subprocess transport.

**Legitimacy = defect (incomplete-implementation of the image).** The on-box MCP server the image
hosts is *designed* to drive the Jira-mutating bridge (`bridge_check_access`, `reconcile`; ADR
0104 / `docs/adr/0104-mcp-on-box.md`), and `acli` is an already-accepted, load-bearing, **pinned**
rebar dependency — README §tools, `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` (`ACLI_VERSION=1.3.19-stable` +
`ACLI_SHA256`), and CI `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` (download + sha256-verify +
install onto PATH). The image build simply omits the install step CI already performs.

**Escalation resolved → mechanical fix, NOT a new-dependency decision.** `acli` is public, free
(no license/account — both arch tarballs downloaded anonymously), single ~15 MB static binary in a
~6 MB tarball, pinnable to `1.3.19-stable` with per-arch sha256. It is not a new external
dependency; it is one already declared and pinned elsewhere in the repo. Per /rebar-debug Step 5
this is the "already-accepted dependency the image omits" case → proceed, no unilateral adoption.

**Portability + arch caveat.** The deploy box is **AL2023 arm64** (`docker-compose.yml:4`), but CI
downloads the **amd64** tarball. A naive copy of the CI amd64 install would ship a non-executable
binary on the arm64 box. The image install therefore selects the arch via Docker's `TARGETARCH`
and pins a per-arch sha256 (amd64 `f29fa8b7…383a6d`, arm64 `72972e74…3674da` for `1.3.19-stable`).
The fix is a plain Dockerfile build step (no CI/deploy-system coupling), so it satisfies
`project.portability`.

**Defect origin (`caused_by`).** Commit `8297083532a3` "Add rebar-mcp HTTP service to the AWS box"
(ticket `fd4a-4e91-f179-4932`) introduced `Dockerfile.mcp` for the on-box MCP server that exposes
the Jira-mutating bridge tools, but never provisioned their `acli` transport. This is an omission
in that originating story's plan (masked until `colourless-hasteless-lamb` wired credentials and
moved the probe past its credential gate to the transport). Close class: `plan_defect`.

Planned fix (Phase 2): add a pinned, arch-aware, sha256-verified `acli` install to
`Dockerfile.mcp` (build-time download via curl, purged after; installed to `/usr/local/bin/acli`
with a `--version` smoke check), plus a manifest test in `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py`
asserting the image declares the pinned install (AC #2). No credential value is used at build time.

comments.body:
## /rebar-debug — Final report (RESOLVED, merged)

**Problem.** The on-box MCP image shipped without the `acli` (Atlassian CLI) binary, so every
Jira-**mutating** bridge op (`bridge_check_access`, `reconcile`) died at the transport with
`[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'acli'` at `STEP_CREATE`. Direct-REST paths were unaffected;
credentials/connectivity/scope were already proven good.

**Proven root cause.** `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp` had no `acli` install step. The Jira
transport spawns `acli` by bare name (`_DEFAULT_ACLI_CMD = ["acli"]` ->
`subprocess.Popen(full_cmd)` in `adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py`, no `which`/abs-path guard), so
an absent binary raises `FileNotFoundError`, surfaced verbatim by `access_check.py:237-241`.

**Proof.** `grep -rn "acli|atlassian" infra/compose/Dockerfile.*` -> nothing. Runtime repro of the
exact string: `Popen(['acli'], env={'PATH':'/nonexistent'})` -> `[Errno 2] No such file or
directory: 'acli'`. Discriminates against the already-excluded rivals (creds `GET /myself`->200,
connectivity, scope).

**Escalation -> resolved as MECHANICAL fix (no unilateral adoption).** `acli` is already an
accepted, pinned rebar dependency -- README, `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` (`ACLI_VERSION=1.3.19-stable`
+ `ACLI_SHA256`), CI `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` (download+verify+install). It is
public/free (both arch tarballs downloaded anonymously, no license/account), a single ~15 MB static
binary in a ~6 MB tarball. Per /rebar-debug Step 5 this is the "already-accepted dependency the
image omits" case, not a new external dependency -> proceed.

**Defect origin.** Commit `8297083532a3` (ticket `fd4a-4e91-f179-4932`, "Add rebar-mcp HTTP service
to the AWS box") introduced `Dockerfile.mcp` but never provisioned the bridge's `acli` transport.
Masked until `colourless-hasteless-lamb` wired credentials and moved the probe past its credential
gate. Close: `caused_by=fd4a-4e91-f179-4932`, class `plan_defect`.

**Test (RED->GREEN).** `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py::test_dockerfile_mcp_provisions_pinned_acli_on_path`
asserts the image declares the pinned, arch-aware, sha256-verified install (host `acli.atlassian.com`,
`ACLI_VERSION`!=latest, `TARGETARCH`, >=2 distinct 64-hex per-arch shas, `sha256sum -c`,
`/usr/local/bin/acli`). Confirmed RED before the fix; GREEN after; mutation-checked (deleting the
install block turns it RED).

**Fix.** `Dockerfile.mcp`: after the OpenSSH RUN, a build step selects arch via Docker `TARGETARCH`,
downloads `acli_${ACLI_VERSION}_linux_{amd64,arm64}.tar.gz`, `sha256sum -c --strict` against the
per-arch pin, extracts only the `acli` binary and `install -m 0755` to `/usr/local/bin/acli`,
smoke-checks `acli --version`, then purges curl and apt lists. amd64 `f29fa8b7...383a6d`,
arm64 `72972e74...3674da` for `1.3.19-stable`.

**Scope & safety / portability.** Deploy box is AL2023 **arm64** (`docker-compose.yml:4`) but CI
downloads amd64 -- the fix is arch-aware so it ships an executable binary on the box. It is a plain
Dockerfile step with no CI/deploy-system coupling -> satisfies `project.portability`. No credentials
used at build time; no secrets in the diff.

**Siblings.** Only the `mcp` container runs Jira-mutating bridge ops (review-bot is code-review
only) -- no sibling images need the same fix.

**Residual risk.** `access_check.py` STEP_CREATE still surfaces a raw `FileNotFoundError` string
rather than a typed "transport unavailable" verdict; hardening tracked as follow-up
`naval-cankered-stud` (ac93-8afd-1666-4866), linked discovered_from this ticket.

**Replication.** Native-arch `docker build` of the acli layer resolves `acli --version` at
`/usr/local/bin/acli`; the pre-fix base image reproduces the `FileNotFoundError`.

**Landed.** Gerrit change **2370** (Change-Id `I4a07c1adb1e4ce70c35753491e5abe2a0864c082`),
PS2: LLM-Review +1 (PASS, advisory-only) + Verified +1 (CI success) -> **Submitted/MERGED** as
`f056344f928d`. Ticket closed.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

The MCP container image installs no `acli` (Atlassian CLI) binary, so every Jira-MUTATING bridge
operation on the deployed box fails at the transport with `[Errno 2] No such file or directory:
'acli'`. The Jira credentials are now correctly wired and authenticate; the binary that would use
them is absent.

## How it was found

Discovered while verifying `colourless-hasteless-lamb`, whose fix wired `JIRA_URL`, `JIRA_USER`,
`JIRA_PROJECT` and `JIRA_API_TOKEN` into the container. That fix moved `bridge_check_access` past
its credential gate and, in doing so, EXPOSED this defect — it was previously masked, because the
probe fail-closed on `missing_credentials` before ever reaching the transport.

## Observed (live, deployed container `rebar-mcp-25ea12c200ae-8092`, one run)

    rebar.bridge_check_access()
    {
      "steps": [
        {
          "step": "STEP_CREATE",
          "passed": false,
          "reason": "exception",
          "detail": "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'acli'"
        }
      ],
      "verdict": "FAIL"
    }

It fails at the FIRST step, `STEP_CREATE`, so `issue_key` stays `None`, the `finally` cleanup is a
no-op and nothing is left behind in Jira. Independently confirmed: a JQL census of
`project = REB AND summary ~ "rebar capability probe"` returned 0 before and 0 after.

## Established by inspection

- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp` installs `git`, `openssh-client`, `ca-certificates`, `uv`, and the
  rebar package (`uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra agents --extra mcp --extra bedrock`). There is
  no `acli` install step.
- `grep -rn "acli\|atlassian" infra/compose/Dockerfile.*` returns NOTHING — no image in the compose
  stack provisions it, not just the mcp one.
- The dependency is real and load-bearing: `applier._load_acli()` resolves the transport, and
  `_backend.py:218` documents the CRUD transport against the remote tracker as
  "today: `acli.AcliClient`".

## Scope of the impact

The credentials themselves are proven good, so this is narrower than "Jira is broken":

- Jira-MUTATING paths are DEAD on the box: `bridge_check_access`, and `reconcile` in
  `bootstrap-strict` / `bootstrap-throttle` / `live`.
- Direct-REST paths still work. Verified live from inside the same container: authenticated
  `GET /rest/api/3/myself` -> 200 and `GET /rest/api/3/project/REB` -> 200, and a JQL search via
  `POST /rest/api/3/search/jql` returned 12 real REB issues.

So the failure is specifically the `acli` subprocess transport, not connectivity, not the
credentials, and not the project scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The mcp container image provisions an `acli` binary on `PATH`, pinned to an explicit version
      (no floating "latest"), with its provenance recorded the way the other pinned tools in the
      image are. — DONE: `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp` installs `acli` to `/usr/local/bin/acli`,
      pinned `ACLI_VERSION=1.3.19-stable` (rejects "latest") with per-arch `sha256sum -c --strict`.
- [x] A test asserts the image declares the `acli` install, so its removal cannot regress silently.
      — DONE: `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py::test_dockerfile_mcp_provisions_pinned_acli_on_path`
      (RED→GREEN; mutation-checked: deleting the install block turns it RED).
- [x] `bridge_check_access` run in the deployed container reaches a verdict WITHOUT a
      `No such file or directory: 'acli'` exception at `STEP_CREATE`. [non-codebase] — VERIFIED by
      replication: a native-arch `docker build` of the acli layer resolves `acli --version` at
      `/usr/local/bin/acli`; the pre-fix base image reproduces the `FileNotFoundError`. Live-box
      re-run of the probe is a deploy step outside this snapshot.
- [x] If `acli` is deliberately NOT to be installed, that decision is recorded instead, together
      with what the bridge transport should be on the box, and the tools that depend on it report a
      typed "transport unavailable" verdict rather than surfacing a raw `FileNotFoundError` detail.
      [non-codebase] — N/A branch: `acli` WAS installed (decision recorded in the Phase 1 RCA
      comment). The typed "transport unavailable" hardening of `access_check.py` is tracked as
      follow-up `naval-cankered-stud` (ac93-8afd-1666-4866), linked discovered_from this ticket.
- [x] No credential value is logged, printed, or committed by the fix or its verification. — DONE:
      the build downloads a public tarball pinned by sha256 and uses no credentials; the diff and
      test contain no secrets.

file_impact.reason: Add pinned, arch-aware, sha256-verified acli (Atlassian CLI) install onto PATH so the Jira-mutating bridge transport resolves in the deployed image
Manifest test asserting the image declares the pinned acli install so it cannot regress silently (AC #2)
